law: Every future component must answer: is this truly Core? If not, which capability owns it? Candidate migrations are MARKED, never silently moved (do-not-break-the-monolith law, §76).

core_components.candidate_capability: core (dispatch); bridge handlers themselves map to owning capabilities
framework.resources (stays Core: every APK needs it)
framework.* families; GL/surface shadows are graphics.opengl candidates
core_components.notes: gl_surface_shadow + surface_view_shadow are the first marked CANDIDATE extractions (only GL apps need them).

core_components.candidate_capability: graphics.font (Core by corpus: nearly all APKs draw text)
network.http (capability, NOT Core — the Mini Browser keeps its closure small)
core_components.notes: Already physically isolated at birth; extraction is trivial when physical modularity lands.

contamination_check: Any new API implementation MUST record which capability owns it and answer: which dependencies does it add, which APKs need it, can it reuse an existing implementation, what does it cost? (S100 §22 law). Recent examples: http_client.cpp born inside network.http capability, physically separate file; crash_forensics born in core/diagnostics.

size_budget.law: A capability implementation must NOT silently inflate Core; every wave reports core_delta/capability_delta/total_runtime_delta.
